title: Implement dynamic presence guard with state carried squared
description:
Create Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.h and Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp implementing the dynamic presence guard that tames accumulating presence-band buildup inside each delay voice's feedback loop.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.h (produced by d.1; reuse its BiquadCoefficients, makePeaking, and per-sample biquad processing rather than duplicating RBJ math)
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp (prepare/reset/process conventions, channel count handling)
- CMakeLists.txt (source list layout only, for reference; do not edit it here)

Required design:
- Class PresenceGuard with a band-pass detector centered on the presence frequency, user-settable within 1.5 kHz to 6 kHz (default 3000 Hz), built from RBJ high-pass and low-pass sections or an RBJ band-pass using the same shared omega0/alpha formulation.
- Detector energy state is carried squared: energy2[n] = alpha*energy2[n-1] + (1 - alpha)*presence*presence. The square root is taken only when the level is read: energy = sqrt(max(energy2, 0.0f) + epsilon). Do not store the square root back into the state, and do not add epsilon into the recursion, so epsilon cannot accumulate into a steady-state bias.
- level_dB = 20*log10(energy + epsilon).
- Excess: u = clamp((level_dB - threshold_dB)/kneeWidth_dB, 0, 1); smoothstep s = 3*u*u - 2*u*u*u.
- cut_dB = -maxCut_dB * s, smoothed, then applied by driving a negative peaking filter (RepeatToneProcessor::makePeaking with gainDb = cut_dB) at the presence frequency.
- Internal defaults: threshold -24 dBFS, knee width 12 dB, detector attack 5 ms, release 120 ms. Attack and release coefficients use alpha = exp(-1.0/(tau*Fs)) with the attack coefficient chosen when the rectified input exceeds the current envelope and the release coefficient otherwise.
- User maximum cut range 0 to 12 dB (default 6 dB). Provide void setEffectiveMaxCutDb (float db) so FOCUS, DEFINITION, and Adaptive Role layering can raise the effective maximum cut later; clamp the effective maximum to [0, 24] dB defensively. This class must not read APVTS or any parameter tree directly.
- Peaking coefficients update at the same bounded control rate as d.1 (recompute in updateCoefficients(), never per sample).

Real-time contract (binding): no heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, GUI calls, buffer resizing, or coefficient-object allocation inside processing methods. All per-channel state is fixed-size and reset in prepare().

Public API to provide (exact names required):
- void prepare (double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize, int numChannels)
- void reset()
- void setPresenceFrequency (float hz)
- void setThresholdDb (float db)
- void setKneeWidthDb (float db)
- void setMaxCutDb (float db)
- void setEffectiveMaxCutDb (float db)
- float processSample (int channel, float x)
- void updateCoefficients()
- float getCurrentCutDb (int channel) const (for tests and telemetry only)
- static float computeCutDb (float levelDb, float thresholdDb, float kneeWidthDb, float maxCutDb) implementing the clamp + smoothstep rule as a pure function so tests can verify the curve directly.

Do not modify DelayVoice or CMakeLists.txt in this task; integration and source registration happen in d.4.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.h declares class PresenceGuard with prepare, reset, setPresenceFrequency, setThresholdDb, setKneeWidthDb, setMaxCutDb, setEffectiveMaxCutDb, processSample, updateCoefficients, getCurrentCutDb, and static computeCutDb

Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp carries detector state as squared energy (energy2 = alpha*energy2 + (1-alpha)*presence*presence) and computes sqrt(max(energy2,0)+epsilon) only at read time, never writing the square root or epsilon back into the state
computeCutDb implements u = clamp((levelDb - thresholdDb)/kneeWidthDb, 0, 1), smoothstep 3u^2 - 2u^3, and cut_dB = -maxCutDb * smoothstep, returning 0 dB at or below threshold
Defaults in Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp are threshold -24 dB, knee 12 dB, attack 5 ms, release 120 ms, and the user max cut is clamped to 0..12 dB with setEffectiveMaxCutDb able to raise it
The cut is applied through an RBJ peaking section obtained from RepeatToneProcessor::makePeaking with negative gain, recomputed only in updateCoefficients()
No heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, or buffer resizing appears in any processing method in Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -I JUCE/modules -I Source Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp succeeds, or the file compiles as part of the existing CMake target once registered in d.4
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: read APVTS or any parameter tree from inside PresenceGuard
store the square root of the detector energy back into the detector state
add epsilon inside the energy recursion
allocate memory, lock, or resize buffers inside processing methods
reference artist or song names in any source file

allowed: choose band-pass detector construction from RBJ high-pass plus low-pass or a single RBJ band-pass
choose internal member naming and per-channel state layout
forbidden: introduce a lookahead or FFT-based detector
apply the cut with a broadband gain instead of a peaking filter
change DelayVoice or plugin processor interfaces
add a new DSP framework or third-party library
